'''Bobby Portis''' (born February 10, 1995) is an American [[basketball]] player who recently closed his college career at the [[University of Arkansas]].  Portis, a 6'11" [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] from [[Little Rock, Arkansas]], was considered one of the top players in college basketball in the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2014–15 season]] and a likely first-round pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web | last = Harris | first = Eric | title = Bobby Portis is Exceeding Expectations | work = [[The Arkansas Traveler (newspaper)|The Arkansas Traveler]] | date = January 14, 2015 | url = http://www.uatrav.com/sports/article_8fc2a222-9ab3-11e4-9a98-c3af15ced85e.html | accessdate = February 28, 2015}}</ref>

Portis played high school basketball at [[Hall High School (Arkansas)|Hall High School]] in Little Rock.  He was a highly-decorated prep player there, earning [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's]] and [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] status and was named [[Mr. Basketball of Arkansas]] in 2013.  Upon committing to Arkansas, Portis became the first in-state McDonald's All-American to sign with the Razorbacks since [[Corliss Williamson]] in 1992 and was considered a key recruit for coach [[Mike Anderson (basketball)|Mike Anderson]]'s rebuild of the program.<ref>{{cite web | last = Tipton | first = Jerry | title = Big man Portis is anchor Arkansas has been seeking for years | work = [[Lexington Herald-Leader]] | date = February 26, 2015 | url = http://www.kentucky.com/2015/02/26/3716163/big-man-portis-is-anchor-arkansas.html | accessdate = February 28, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last = Medcalf | first = Myron | title = Basketball can change Bobby Portis' life | work = [[ESPN.com]] | date = December 30, 2014 | url = http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/12092388/arkansas-bobby-portis-overcomes-poverty-violence-prosper | accessdate = February 28, 2015}}</ref>

As a freshman, Portis averaged 12.3 [[points per game|points]], 6.8 [[Rebounds per game|rebounds]] and 1.6 [[Blocked shot|blocks]] per game.  He was named to the [[Southeastern Conference]] All-Freshman team and second-team All-SEC.

In his sophomore season, Portis was named to the preseason All-SEC team<ref>{{cite web | last = Harper| first = Doc | title = Bobby Portis Named 1st Team All-SEC; Razorbacks Picked 3rd In Preseason Poll | work = [[SBNation.com]] | date = October 22, 2014 | url = http://www.arkansasfight.com/2014/10/22/7039537/bobby-portis-named-1st-team-all-sec-razorbacks-picked-3rd-in-preseason-poll| accessdate = February 28, 2015}}</ref> and led the Razorbacks to a top 25 ranking.  During his second and final season, Portis averaged 17.5 points, 8.9 rebounds, 1.4 blocks, 1.2 assists, and 1.1 steals per game.  He was named one of 20 finalists for the [[John R. Wooden Award]] for national college player of the year, one of only two players from the SEC.<ref>{{cite web | last = | first = | title = Cauley-Stein, Portis on Wooden Award late season top-20 | work = [[Southeastern Conference]] | date = February 11, 2015 | url = http://www.secsports.com/article/12310404/two-wooden-award-top-20 | accessdate = February 28, 2015}}</ref>

On March 10, 2015, Portis was selected as the SEC Player of the Year by the league's coaches.  This marks the first time an Arkansas Razorback was selected since [[Corliss Williamson]] won the award back-to-back during the [[1993–94 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings|1993–94]] and [[1994–95 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings|1994–95]] seasons.
